A discounted cash flow analysis places the intrinsic value of Bajaj Auto Ltd at Rs 15,929 per share against a market price of Rs 11,700 [E46], offering a robust margin of safety of 26.6% [E47]. This valuation gap is further highlighted by a reverse DCF, which reveals that the current market price implies an earnings growth rate of just 12.8%, well below the 17.0% assumed in the base case [E48]. Supporting this growth potential is the company's superior operational performance, demonstrated by a return on assets (ROA) of 14.96% that far exceeds the sector benchmark of 5.89% [E8]. Reflecting this strong fundamental backing, the stock exhibits powerful market momentum, trading at 95% of the way up its 52-week range [E5]. Conceded: the company trades at a premium relative to its peers, with a P/E of 27.83x and a P/B of 8.28x compared to sector benchmarks of 25.89x and 2.83x [E6] [E7], while its price growth of 26% has outpaced its 5-year profit growth of 17% [E57].

Conceded: a discounted cash flow suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 15,929 against the market price of Rs 11,700 [E46], leaving a 26.6% margin of safety [E47]. However, relying on this model ignores the severe warning from the scanX signal engine that price has outpaced fundamentals with 26% price growth versus 17% profit growth over 5 years [E57]. The bull highlights a reverse DCF implying a 12.8% growth rate against a 17.0% base case [E48], but this still demands double-digit growth while the stock sits at 95% of its 52-week range [E5], leaving very little room for execution error. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the stark valuation disconnect shown by a price-to-book ratio of 8.28x or 8.42x against a sector benchmark of just 2.83x [E2] [E7]. As the insider-bias checklist explicitly warns, a rich P/E of 27.8x and a high P/B mean a market-beating chart does not make a rich entry safe, because the current price already discounts a heavy amount of good news [E6] [E71].
